approach.method_basis: The Parent builds a persistent tree of de novo graph edits, buys the first unscored frontier directly, and backs each accepted return onto its exact route. It retains both mean and best completed returns. Selection shares count-weighted best returns and completed/pending support across structurally similar siblings. After a strict accepted improvement, it restarts from the new global incumbent as one fresh root with its original accepted receipt as context, keeping the global accepted archive while discarding the old episode topology.
approach.novelty: Remove sibling sharing only from decisions below the virtual root, so each deeper occurrence competes using its own best return and its own completed/pending counts. Root competition continues to share information. This isolates the conditional influence of deeper sharing on the successful fresh-root host. The currently bound siblings instead retain a second origin or exclude a proven exhausted action class; this Child changes neither origin membership nor eligibility. No completed same-Parent sibling is supplied.

observed_bottleneck: The retained deeper sharing consumer has a large but unpriced influence on the actual fresh-root Parent n-e4b751133c75. Its complete Search mean is 0.49949631467224465 (standard deviation 0.014066662744436314), with +0.15139519654635733 versus its code Parent n-85acb9fe7124, while the separate formal Anchor remains at 0.607030316211131. Successful lifecycle feedback does not show that a neighboring occurrence supplies useful return support. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen permitted Parent Search logs and trajectories reproduces 5109 diagonal-peak versus inherited shared-peak choice differences among 7043 deeper decisions, with positive off-diagonal completed support in 5462 decisions. The changed replay decisions participate in 2882 distinct actual Parent paid terminal paths; these are receipts from the sharing law, not outcomes for alternative diagonal actions. All 4891 root choices are outside this removal. The Parent has 114 fresh-root promotions, 4350 paid optimizer receipts, full incumbent mass 4.365063054449033 and late-half mass 1.3674630683963998. The older n-4e4e248bd6bd sharing result changes roots and deeper decisions jointly on a mean/rollout host; n-5cc901d1a9e3 then changes mean exploitation to peaks, and n-85acb9fe7124 changes the purchase frontier. None answers this current deeper-only contrast. Exact per-cell audits and underlying Search logs/trajectories are cited together in declared_parameters.planning_evidence_sources; every input hash is recorded in policy/scratch/r0055-03-improve-L01/audit-summary.json and its fifteen per-cell audits.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review and its actual recorded queries; no new search query was issued. The primary IJCAI PDF was opened directly to check the distinction between kernel value estimation and density. B1 is the reproduced 5109/7043 action-only replay on the actual Parent, not a reward prediction. B3 is the changed host: direct frontier feedback, maxima and fresh roots may alter the utility of statistical sharing, while the earlier all-level mean-sharing result cannot isolate it here. The one registered deeper diagonal-peak removal is therefore testable with passive inherited rows, untouched root/lifecycle laws and a complete signed endpoint interpretation. Source findings provide context only, so adoptions remain empty.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen ticket isolates an existing consumer because a new maximum-preserving replay verifies extensive deeper choice exposure on the successful fresh-root Parent. Historical joint root/deeper sharing, the peak-statistic result and lifecycle result do not identify this contribution. The change removes off-diagonal terms without borrowing a new external method. No asset, package or preparation input is introduced.

hypothesis: Remove active off-diagonal sibling-kernel influence only when parent_id != 0. For deeper occurrence i, active D_i=N_i, S_i=W_i, B_i=N_i*M_i when N_i>0 (zero otherwise), P_i=O_i, shared_Q_i=W_i/N_i when N_i>0, and Qbest_i=M_i when N_i>0. If N_i=0 retain the inherited neutral exploitation default. Keep unvisited priority D_i+P_i==0, exploration beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D_i+P_i)), and earliest-occurrence ties. The virtual-root rows keep the complete original count-Tanimoto weighted peak rule including initial-forest competition. Stored route N/W/Q/M/O, maximum receipt identity, returned-receipt lists, raw-count widening, direct-frontier purchase and accepted-incumbent fresh-root lifecycle remain inherited. This is one conditional removal of deeper shared value and completed/pending density together; it does not separately identify those mediators.

finding_summary.headline: Deeper sharing removal executed faithfully and lowered mean score by 0.0523
finding_summary.insights:
Fresh-root feedback does not make deeper sharing redundant under these conditions. Removing its combined value and visitation-density influence saves many internal failed attempts and produces more frequent small improvements, yet loses enough larger improvements to lower every seed macro. This distinguishes successful removal from score success: the mechanism is confirmed, the working non-inferiority expectation is contradicted, and the signed contribution finding favors the presence of deeper sharing on this specific host. It does not identify whether shared best returns or exploration density supplies that benefit, and it says nothing separately about root sharing or whether the broader tree approach should end.

The search still reaches broad scaffold diversity: distinct typed scaffolds increase from 1,704 to 1,829. However, within-announcement similarity rises from 0.492 to 0.566, and the late-half value reaches 0.580. There is no evidence of global scaffold collapse; the limiting behavior is conversion of plentiful graph variants into large useful gains. Tiny fragments decrease, but oversized products and oxygen–oxygen linkages increase. The molecular assessment finds inconsistent preservation of favorable polar-group and ring relationships, including less conventional arrangements among the poorer docking leaders. A graph proposal method that can vary topology and linkers while preserving those relationships could address this limitation. These chemistry associations do not establish the cause of the removal loss or guarantee that such a method would improve scores. Parent logs lack separate proposal and diagnostic clocks, so the runtime change cannot be assigned to the selector alone.
finding_summary.results: The removal worked: all 26,480 deeper selection rows used only their own completed and pending evidence, with no formula or accounting errors and unchanged root and restart laws. It changed 2,938 of 4,105 deeper decisions; 2,471 of 4,350 accepted optimizer outcomes passed through changed choices, with exposure in every task/seed cell. Across the complete three-seed panel, mean score fell from 0.499496 to 0.447190, a paired loss of 0.052307. All three seed macros fell; seven task/seed endpoints improved and eight worsened. The largest consistent loss was on drd2_docking, whose task mean fell by 0.258604. Incumbent improvements became more frequent, from 148 to 192, but their total gain fell from 4.3651 to 3.5805; late-half gain also fell, from 1.3675 to 1.0134. That loss meets the preregistered criterion for positive conditional contribution of retained deeper sharing. The separate formal Anchor mean remains 0.607030.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and nitrogenous products retain amines and carbonyls, but strained scaffolds, reactive bonds and size extremes persist.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied task and all frozen Search seeds. Child evaluation and Parent pairing are both complete in context.comparison; all 15 trusted Child staging trajectories and all 15 published Parent trajectories exist and were read, with 300 rows and 290 optimizer rows per cell. No task or Parent comparison is missing. Across 4350 accepted optimizer rows, the Child has 4038 ring-bearing and 3696 aromatic-bearing products, versus 3762 and 3407 in the Parent. The molecular digest independently reports ring-closure-token rates 0.8724–0.954 and aromatic-token rates 0.6241–0.9287; these are proportions of SMILES with those tokens, not proportions of atoms. The chemistry includes aryl and heteroaryl carboxamides, cyclic amines, hydrazine/urea-like rings, sulfur linkers, polycarbonyl rings, and heavily halogenated or bridged frameworks. Ordinary-looking examples coexist with highly strained or reactive-looking ones. The Child spans 1–119 heavy atoms, with median 27, compared with Parent median 26. It reduces the below-six-heavy-atom tail from 425 to 209 rows but increases the above-fifty tail from 301 to 381. Distinct nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1829/1324 versus 1704/1240; this is broad graph coverage with seed-specific motif concentration, not proof of useful medicinal diversity. Heteroatom–halogen adjacency appears in 373 Child rows versus 832 Parent rows, while O–O adjacency appears in 434 versus 174. Those bond counts flag structures for inspection; they do not measure instability or synthetic feasibility. Every task has zero tetrahedral stereochemical-token rate. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, and drug-likeness weak despite substantial medicinal-chemistry fragments. No synthesis, stability, potency, binding-mode or component-attribution claim follows from these scores. Numeric structural summaries are direct RDKit readings of accepted trajectories, with initial molecules excluded. Provenance is recorded in policy/scratch/r0055-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and the per-seed per-task audit JSON files in that directory. Each audit cites a byte-identical Child snapshot under its trajectory-inputs directory and the actual published Parent file under nodes/n-e4b751133c75/seed-N/trajectories. The audit preserves the exact original Child absolute staging path from the immutable request, its SHA256, the snapshot SHA256 equality and the request SHA256. Snapshots do not replace the frozen request as citation authority; no future Child archive path is treated as an existing source.

per_task.generated_character: Most products carry aromatic rings, carboxamides and nitrogen heterocycles, with methoxy, methyl, halogen and sulfur substitutions. The 870 optimizer rows have median 25 heavy atoms; 830 are ring-bearing and 808 aromatic-bearing. The seed 0 leader is a relatively conventional fluoro/methoxy/methyl indole-acetamide joined to a fluoropyridyl group: 25 heavy atoms, three rings, score 0.40497388700123543. The seed 1 leader is a compact bridged unsaturated heterocycle bearing an N-methyl group, vinyl ether and pyridyl carboxamide, score 0.4451945621839941. The seed 2 leader has an enol substituent, cyclic imine, thiol, methylpyridyl group and carboxamide attached to a bridged aromatic fragment; it has 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, score 0.4708092433701816. The latter two frameworks raise substantially greater synthetic questions than the seed 0 indole derivative. Parent leaders also carry compact polycyclic aromatic/amide or sulfur/nitrogen frameworks; the Child has not discovered ring chemistry from scratch.
liabilities: Bridged aromatic fragments, cyclic imine/enol tautomerism and thiol substitution make several leaders chemically less straightforward than their score suggests.
An N-fluoro carboxamide occurs among high examples; terminal proposals also include unusual sulfur–oxygen and oxygen–chlorine connections.
There are 31 below-six-heavy-atom and 14 above-fifty-heavy-atom optimizer rows, and no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry.
missing_features: The higher-scoring amide/heteroaryl arrangements are not consistently retained during size and scaffold edits; low examples can lose them entirely or bury them inside very large assemblies.

The best examples do not supply a coherent set of less strained, conventional ring/linker alternatives around the same observed polar arrangement. No unseen objective-specific pharmacophore can be inferred from this evidence.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed upper range associates compact multi-ring structures with amide and heteroatom functionality. Methane, hydrogen peroxide and vinyl fluoride score zero, but some enormous linked aromatic assemblies also score zero, so neither shrinking nor adding aromatic matter alone describes the gradient. The digest median is 0.135626. Parent seed maxima are 0.42348216717712805, 0.42348216717712805 and 0.4031937733859023; the Child chemical changes are favorable in some seeds and unfavorable in another. The leading structures do not isolate any particular enol, thiol or bridged-ring benefit.

per_task.generated_character: This set is aromatic, sulfur-rich and frequently halogenated, with methoxy/acetate decorations and both conventional and unusual heteroatom linkers. Median size is 29 heavy atoms; 821 of 870 optimizer rows contain rings and 792 contain aromatic atoms. The seed 1 leader is a 30-heavy-atom two-ring pyridyl/phenyl assembly with thioether–methylene–aniline linkage, methylthio groups, methoxy, acetate, fluorines and a methylene-imine substituent (0.615283898575717). The seed 0 leader is a 30-heavy-atom fused heteroaromatic acyl-sulfur framework with an S–N connection and an O–O-containing ring (0.5923392612859097). The seed 2 leader is much larger: 54 heavy atoms and ten perceived rings, with fused nitrogen heterocycles and O–O-containing aromatic ring connectivity (0.593309605117599). Synthetic coherence is especially questionable in the latter two families.
liabilities: There are 187 above-fifty-heavy-atom products and 40 below-six-heavy-atom fragments.
O–O adjacency occurs in 307 optimizer rows, versus 75 in the Parent; examples include explicitly peroxide-containing rings and unusual aromatic O–O connectivity.
Methylene imines, nitroso substitutions, sulfur-rich linkers and heavily decorated polycycles complicate stability and route planning.
missing_features: Controlled ring and linker alternatives that preserve the better-scoring aromatic decoration pattern are inconsistent; a substantial part of the set instead expands into fused or linked oversized systems.

The high-score examples do not establish a stable, readily interpretable linker series free of peroxide-like, S–N or imine complications; their absence is a chemical coverage gap, not a measured score requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Several chemically minimal products, including dimethyl ether, a small imine and difluorine, receive exactly 0.5. Their common floor supplies no evidence of useful target chemistry. Decorated aromatic assemblies reach about 0.59–0.615, while the listed large chlorinated, ester-bearing oxygen heterocycle scores 0.2653483723586522. The score is therefore sensitive to arrangement, not merely the presence of rings or substituents. Parent seed maxima 0.5852068576121547, 0.6354531001589825 and 0.581008100810081 likewise show mixed structural outcomes. The Parent seed 1 leader is a substituted heteroaryl/ether assembly that itself contains an N–Br bond, so its higher score does not validate synthetic quality either.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by large halogenated aromatic frameworks with aminoalkyl, imine/enamine, phenol, ether or N–O functionality. Median size is 35 heavy atoms, versus Parent 30; 816 of 870 Child products are ring-bearing and 794 aromatic-bearing. The seed 0 leader is a 34-heavy-atom, six-ring brominated polycycle with a primary aminomethyl substituent and phenol (0.7050035340559307). The seed 1 leader has 30 heavy atoms and a chloroaromatic core bearing an enol, an amino-substituted alkene, a terminal dimethylamine and an aryl-O-N linkage leading to a small bridged aromatic fragment (0.6957092845559729). The seed 2 leader is a 28-heavy-atom substituted aryl/bridged ring system with exocyclic imines and fluoroalkyl functionality (0.5715673728287868). Amines are present; lack of nitrogen is not the problem.
liabilities: The 108 above-fifty-heavy-atom Child products double the Parent count of 54; forty Child products are below six heavy atoms.
Heavy bromination, unusually bridged aromatic subgraphs, enol/imino tautomerism and N–O linkages make several leaders questionable as conventional medicinal molecules.
Complex saturated and bridged products carry no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry; a recorded docking score is not evidence of a defined stereoisomer or experimental binding.
missing_features: The leading Child molecules do not consistently recover the relatively conventional saturated-ring amine/linker relationships visible in the higher-scoring Parent exemplars. Their presence elsewhere in the population is not ruled out.
The observed polar/aromatic combinations lack systematic alternatives that vary spacing and ring saturation without simultaneously adding strained bridges, imines or heavy halogen substitution.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Accessible amino groups combined with hydrophobic ring surfaces characterize several upper examples, whereas the listed small carbamate/imide and acylated quinoline-like product score 0.0007816592771166815 and 0.00002455818463669451, respectively. Large aromatic thioamide/hydrazine products can also score poorly. This supports arrangement and accessibility as observed associations, not a universal amine rule. Published Parent leaders score 0.9190747819767275, 0.9687642535682931 and 0.8602533326723711, and show aryl surfaces coupled to saturated cyclic tertiary amines or aminoalkyl groups. The Child leaders retain related polar/hydrophobic ingredients but more often place them in brominated bridged frameworks or imine/enamine/N–O chemistry. Neither docking validity nor a binding mechanism is established by this comparison.

per_task.generated_character: These products combine phenyl/heteroaryl rings with nitrogen-rich saturated or unsaturated rings, cyclic urea/imide-like carbonyls, alkoxy groups and alkyl substituents. Median size is 31 heavy atoms; 812 of 870 products contain rings and 759 aromatic atoms. The seed 0 leader is a five-ring aryl/heteroaryl ether framework bearing an N–N-containing saturated ring (28 heavy atoms, 0.1839069610833919). The seed 1 leader has four rings and 35 heavy atoms: a bicyclic nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl system with an N–N-linked ethoxy/methylphenyl substituent and an amino-substituted nonaromatic diene ring (0.18851647550933462). The seed 2 leader is a more readily recognizable aryl-substituted fused nitrogen heterocycle with two carbonyls, N-methyl groups, phenyl, propyl and hydroxymethyl substituents (30 heavy atoms, 0.18354739684687046).
liabilities: Several upper examples contain hydrazine-like N–N connections, enlarged unsaturated rings or N-fluoro substitution; not every N–N bond in this set is intrinsically problematic, since aromatic diazoles are also present.
There are 37 tiny fragments and 63 above-fifty-heavy-atom assemblies despite strong overall ring coverage.
Substituted saturated ring systems are represented without explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry.
missing_features: Coherent alternatives that preserve the observed aryl/carbonyl/nitrogen relationships while changing ring architecture remain inconsistent; some edits merely create further N–N linkages or ring expansions.

A clear, reproducible structural route beyond the modest upper score range is absent from these examples. The unseen feature needed for a substantially higher value cannot be specified from the available molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Higher examples retain multi-ring carbon/nitrogen frameworks and multiple polar functions, whereas methane, oxygen halides and chloromethanol score zero and the small hydroxylated urea O=C(NO)NO scores 0.007937507937511907. Yet the entire upper range is modest: the digest median is 0.145957 and maximum 0.18851647550933462. Parent maxima are 0.1678386594791329, 0.18484422002677828 and 0.19720265943665388; the first is an initial molecule, not a Parent-generated discovery. Broad ring rearrangement in the Child therefore does not demonstrate a consistent improvement in useful chemical arrangement. This evidence does not identify a missing named scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: This is the least uniformly aromatic set: 543 of 870 optimizer products contain aromatic atoms, while 759 contain rings. Median size is 23 heavy atoms. The seed 0 leader is a 20-heavy-atom pyrrole/acetyl-containing structure with methoxy, chloromethoxy and imine/enamine functionality (0.22314763342772323). The seed 1 leader has 24 heavy atoms and no aromatic atoms: a fluorinated cyclic vicinal diketone linked through a cyclopropene to an unsaturated amino chain bearing an aminooxy terminus (0.4874850373972224). The seed 2 leader is a 23-heavy-atom fused nitrogen-rich aromatic carbonyl framework with methoxy, thiol and methyl substitutions (0.3470520225937146). These are distinct compact polar chemotypes, not one converged scaffold; the cyclopropene/diketone/enamine combination is especially challenging to interpret as a stable, synthetically straightforward product.
liabilities: The highest example combines a strained cyclopropene, a vicinal diketone, several fluoro substituents, enamine functionality and an aminooxy N–O bond.
Other upper examples contain imines or thiols; very large recombinants remain accessible even though only nine optimizer products exceed fifty heavy atoms.
Sixty-one products have fewer than six heavy atoms, and all products lack explicit tetrahedral stereochemical tokens.
missing_features: The upper compact polar arrangements lack a demonstrated set of conventional, less reactive ring/linker alternatives with comparable observed scores; aromaticity itself is clearly not obligatory for the upper Child example.
Defined stereochemical states of the substituted cyclic products are absent. The trajectories do not show that stereochemical specification would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Compact heteroatom-rich frameworks outperform enormous oxygen-rich/aromatic recombinants in the listed examples: a large acetal-rich assembly scores zero and several large linked aromatic products are effectively at the lower end, while the digest median is 0.000625. Very small products are also poor, so a simple size reduction rule is unsupported. A close fluorinated pair scores 0.4874850373972224 and 0.38751501057137566 when the cyclic diketone carbon carries two versus one fluorine substituents; that is a local association, not a general instruction to fluorinate. Parent seed maxima are 0.4230032077811577, 0.35855114551835887 and 0.36108629330282105, and include hydrazine/thione, N-fluoro and amino-acetal chemistry. Neither side supplies a uniformly conventional chemical solution.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-3f6f7c11f468; complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, Research in Depth profile epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 accepted observations per session. Comparison is the published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Audit: policy/scratch/r0055-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json. Among 4350 accepted optimizer records, below-six-heavy-atom products decrease from Parent 425 to Child 209, but above-fifty-heavy-atom products increase from 301 to 381. Upper examples often retain compact connected polar/ring arrangements, while low examples include both tiny fragments and oversized linked assemblies. This is an output association, not attribution to a controller component.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size changes do not consistently preserve a useful connected ring and polar-group framework.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide contraction, expansion and scaffold rearrangement choices that can preserve existing functional-group relationships, using only current-session accepted feedback to discover useful scale. These observations do not justify a universal size floor, size ceiling or a guaranteed benefit from either.

Comparison is the published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Audit: policy/scratch/r0055-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json. Child heteroatom–halogen adjacency falls to 373 records from Parent 832, but O–O adjacency rises to 434 from 174. Upper examples still include N-fluoro amide, sulfur–nitrogen, peroxide-like, hydroxylamine/aminooxy, enol/imine and bridged aromatic chemistry; conventional indole-amide and aryl-carbonyl examples also occur. Bond adjacency is descriptive and is not a reactivity or synthetic-accessibility score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Promising chemical neighbourhoods lack consistent conventional alternatives to unusual heteroatom linkages and strained ring connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically conservative bond, linker and ring alternatives around accepted promising graphs so that conventional chemistry can compete within the same task-local feedback loop. Do not infer that deleting every flagged bond improves a score, and do not convert these associations into component-level claims.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-3f6f7c11f468; complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, Research in Depth profile epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 accepted observations per session. Comparison is the published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Audit: policy/scratch/r0055-03-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json. Child nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffold counts are 1829/1324 versus Parent 1704/1240, and several leaders contain accessible amino groups or carbonyl-bearing heterocycles alongside aromatic surfaces. Other variants block nitrogen in acyl groups, replace amino topology with imines, lose the ring framework or greatly enlarge it. The Parent also reaches relatively conventional saturated-ring amine arrangements with high observed values. These examples show inconsistent retention, not a universal absence of amines or rings, and do not isolate which structural difference matters.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring diversity is broad, but changes do not consistently retain favorable spatial relationships between polar groups and aromatic surfaces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer topology and linker transformations that can vary saturation, orientation and ring connections while retaining chemically meaningful polar-group relationships. Let accepted observations within each fresh session determine their value; a fixed imported pharmacophore or objective-specific recipe is unsupported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-3f6f7c11f468; complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, Research in Depth profile epoch 1, batch size 10 and 300 accepted observations per session. All five digest stereocentre-token rates are zero, and all 4350 Child optimizer SMILES lack explicit tetrahedral stereochemical tokens, as do the Parent records. Actual examples include multiply substituted saturated rings, bridges, aminoacetals and fluorinated cyclic carbonyl systems. This is a representation gap; the observed scores do not establish a preferred stereoisomer or a benefit from specifying one.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted saturated and bridged structures do not distinguish chemically meaningful tetrahedral stereochemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and distinguish supported stereochemical states when graph edits introduce or retain stereogenic environments, subject to the existing identity and evaluation contract. Resolve their relevance only through legal current-session observations; do not choose stereochemistry from benchmark identity or claim an unmeasured performance gain.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
